events.title: Henry VIII Marries Catherine Parr
events.description: At Hampton Court Palace, King Henry VIII of England married Catherine Parr. She was his sixth and last wife.
events.significance: Catherine outlived Henry. She helped reconcile him with his daughters Mary and Elizabeth, which shaped the royal succession.

events.title: Alexander Hamilton Dies After His Duel with Aaron Burr
events.description: Alexander Hamilton, the first U.S. Secretary of the Treasury, died of the wound he received in a duel with Vice President Aaron Burr. The duel took place the day before.
events.significance: Hamilton built the foundations of the American financial system. His death ended one of the young republic's greatest political rivalries and badly damaged Burr's career.

events.title: U.S. Forces Invade Canada at Windsor
events.description: During the War of 1812, American troops crossed the Detroit River into Upper Canada near Windsor, Ontario.
events.significance: The invasion was an early attempt to take British North America. It ended in failure, and the campaign helped shape Canadian resistance and identity.

events.title: Henry David Thoreau Is Born
events.description: The writer, naturalist and leading transcendentalist was born in Concord, Massachusetts.
events.significance: Thoreau wrote Walden and the essay on civil disobedience. His ideas about simple living and nonviolent resistance still influence environmental and protest movements.

events.title: Hezbollah Attack Sparks the Israel–Lebanon War
events.description: Hezbollah forces crossed the Israel–Lebanon border and attacked Israeli military positions. They also fired rockets and mortars at Israeli towns.
events.significance: The attack began a war that lasted about five weeks. It caused heavy casualties and destruction, mostly in Lebanon, and it reshaped regional politics.
